tasks.title: Add lean-mechanic tuning knobs to VehicleStats
tasks.description: Add exported fields for the landing/impact lean mechanic: max lean angle clamp, landing-angle trigger threshold, impact-speed trigger threshold, self-correction duration/rate.
tasks.details: Same pattern as existing air_control/drift_grip knobs — exported vars with doc comments explaining tuning intent, defaults chosen for arcade feel not simulation accuracy.
tasks.test_strategy: .tres opens in Inspector with new fields editable.

tasks.title: Add deterministic landing/impact lean to VehicleController
tasks.description: On airborne-to-grounded transition or hard lateral impact, sample touchdown angle vs ground normal, impact speed along a lateral axis, and current speed ONCE per event; compute a bounded pitch/roll lean from a designed curve over those sampled values and apply as a rotational offset that decays to level over the configured duration.
tasks.details: Must NOT derive lean from raw per-frame move_and_slide() contact data — that path is non-deterministic (contact-order dependency, sub-pixel contact-point variance, floor-snap flicker between grounded/airborne, discrete-time tunneling push-out impulses, multi-body collision order). Same sampled inputs must always produce the same lean output. Clamp max lean well short of any stuck/upside-down state so it composes safely with the stuck/flip recovery tasks.
tasks.test_strategy: Same sampled inputs (angle/speed) always produce same lean output across runs; lean visibly decays back to level within the configured duration.

tasks.title: Surface lean state in debug HUD
tasks.description: Extend the debug overlay to show current lean angle and the last trigger cause (landing-angle vs impact-speed) for hand-feel tuning.
tasks.details: Read VehicleController state only, same pattern as the existing last_input readout — do not poll Input.* directly from the debug layer (Architecture Decision 01).
tasks.test_strategy: F3 overlay shows lean angle climb/decay and correct trigger label during a ramp landing.

tasks.title: GdUnit4 test: lean determinism, decay, and clamp
tasks.description: Feed fixed sampled inputs (touchdown angle, impact speed, current speed) via scene_runner; assert identical inputs always produce identical lean output, lean decays to level within the configured duration, and lean never exceeds the clamp.
tasks.details: Covers the determinism guarantee that is the actual design justification for allowing lean at all (Guardrail 1 reproducibility, not a bespoke visual telegraph).

tasks.title: Hand-feel test lean on ramp landings
tasks.description: Manually verify on test_track.tscn's ramp that lean reads as a consequence of a reckless landing (not random), self-corrects fast enough to not feel like lost control, and doesn't read as a bug.
tasks.details: No file change — tuning/verification pass only, adjust VehicleStats knobs from task 1 by feel.

tasks.title: Update vehicles.md to reflect bounded-lean behavior
tasks.description: Rewrite the Technical Implementation section's COM-anchoring claim to describe the shipped bounded/self-correcting lean instead of an absolute never-tips guarantee.
tasks.details: vehicles.md currently states COM is anchored specifically to prevent tipping over — that's now inaccurate once the lean mechanic ships and needs to match actual behavior.

tasks.title: Detect stuck/flipped vehicle state
tasks.description: Track sustained abnormal state — orientation past a threshold or near-zero velocity with no valid floor contact — held for N seconds, and emit a stuck/flip signal when the threshold is crossed. Track last-known valid grounded position as the future recovery point.
tasks.details: Timer-gated to avoid false positives from normal airtime. This is a safety net for physics edge cases (tunneling, wedged geometry, multi-body pileups) that the lean clamp in task 2 doesn't fully rule out.
tasks.test_strategy: Force the car into a wedged/flipped test position in a scratch scene; confirm signal fires after the timer, not instantly.

tasks.title: Recover from stuck/flip: reset near last valid position
tasks.description: On the stuck/flip signal, reset the vehicle to the last valid grounded position plus a small offset, zero velocity and angular velocity, with a brief invulnerability window.
tasks.details: Matches the existing Comic Respawn convention already documented in vehicles.md (<=1.5s, instant control back). Prefer an in-place transform/velocity reset over deleting and recreating the node — recreation loses input_source/stats wiring and connected signals unless carefully restored, while a reset achieves the identical player-visible outcome.
tasks.test_strategy: Trigger task 7's stuck signal manually; confirm car reappears near last valid ground position, controllable immediately.

tasks.title: GdUnit4 test: stuck detection and recovery
tasks.description: Simulate a stuck condition (fixed bad orientation/velocity held past the timer), assert recovery fires, position resets near the tracked last-valid point, velocity/angular velocity zero, and the stuck flag clears.

tasks.title: Debug hotkey: manually trigger stuck/flip recovery
tasks.description: Add a debug-only hotkey, gated behind GameConfig.debug_mode (same pattern as the existing F3 telemetry toggle), that calls the recovery routine from task 8 directly on the local player's vehicle.
tasks.details: Expose the recovery routine as a public method on VehicleController so the debug layer can call it without the controller polling Input itself (Architecture Decision 01).
tasks.test_strategy: With debug mode on, press the hotkey mid-drive; car resets near last valid position same as an automatic recovery would.

tasks.title: Add coast-down deceleration when throttle is released
tasks.description: Add a coast_deceleration knob to VehicleStats and apply it in VehicleController when throttle is 0, so releasing the gas scrubs speed instead of holding constant velocity forever.
tasks.details: Currently current_speed only changes under nonzero throttle input, so releasing the pedal acts like cruise control. coast_deceleration should be weaker than braking_force so active braking still feels stronger than just lifting off. Independent of the lean/flip tasks.
tasks.test_strategy: Release throttle mid-drive: speed visibly drops off over ~1-2s instead of holding flat; braking still decelerates faster than coasting.

tasks.title: Add balance-tilt tuning knobs to VehicleStats
tasks.description: Add exported fields for the continuous corner-support balance tilt: max balance tilt angle, corner raycast probe distance, and a smoothing/response-rate knob for how quickly tilt follows changing support.
tasks.details: Separate knobs from the existing event-lean fields (max_lean_angle etc.) rather than reusing them -- balance tilt is a continuous, always-on function of support state while event lean is a decaying one-shot response to a trigger; sharing a cap would couple two mechanics with different tuning needs. Same doc-comment style as existing knobs (units stated, tuning intent stated).

tasks.title: Compute continuous balance tilt from four-corner support raycasts
tasks.description: Cast four downward raycasts from the vehicle footprint's corners (derived from the collision shape's extents, oriented by current yaw) each grounded physics frame; weight how many corners have ground under them and compute a continuous tilt value toward the unsupported side(s), clamped to the new max balance tilt angle.
tasks.details: Store the result in new fields (e.g. _balance_pitch_deg / _balance_roll_deg) separate from the existing event-lean fields -- do not overwrite _lean_pitch_deg/_lean_roll_deg here; composing the two is a distinct task (see dependent task). All four corners supported (or within a near-full-support threshold) must yield zero balance tilt. A fully airborne car (zero corners supported) must not apply balance tilt at all -- that's the existing airborne/falling code path, a different case from partial support while grounded. Must never touch self/transform.basis -- raycast results only ever feed the visual-mesh-only tilt fields, preserving the yaw-only collision body invariant from task 2.
tasks.test_strategy: Manual scratch-scene check: park the car with a known corner hanging off a ledge, confirm the computed balance tilt fields move off zero in the expected direction; all-four-supported case stays at zero.

tasks.title: Resolve composition of balance tilt with event-triggered lean on the visual mesh
tasks.description: Decide and implement how the continuous balance tilt combines with the existing event-triggered _lean_pitch_deg/_lean_roll_deg when writing the visual mesh's rotation each frame -- they currently both would target the same MeshInstance3D.rotation.
tasks.details: This is the trickiest open design question flagged during scoping, called out as its own reviewable decision rather than folded silently into the raycast task. Candidate approaches: additive blend of both values before writing to the mesh; suppressing balance tilt for a short window right after an event-lean trigger so they don't visibly fight; or balance tilt taking priority during sustained grounded state since it reflects an ongoing physical fact while event lean is inherently transient. Whichever is chosen must be justified against Guardrail 1 (reproducible, not random-feeling) and must not reintroduce the original bug (car resting precariously with zero tilt) or a new one (mesh visibly fighting itself between two competing rotations right after a landing on an edge).
tasks.test_strategy: Manual scratch-scene check: trigger an event lean, then let the car settle into a partial-support resting state, confirm the mesh rotation transitions smoothly rather than snapping or oscillating between the two sources.

tasks.title: Surface balance-tilt state in debug HUD
tasks.description: Extend the debug overlay to show current balance-tilt magnitude and how many footprint corners are currently supported, for hand-feel tuning.
tasks.details: Same pattern as the existing lean readout in debug_overlay.gd -- read VehicleController state only, no Input polling from the debug layer (Architecture Decision 01).
tasks.test_strategy: F3 overlay shows balance-tilt magnitude and supported-corner count change live while driving onto a ledge.

tasks.title: GdUnit4 tests: balance-tilt support states
tasks.description: Cover three support states: all four corners supported yields zero balance tilt; a controlled partial-support scenario (e.g. car positioned so only some corners are over a floor edge) produces a tilt in the correct direction bounded by the clamp; a fully airborne car (zero corners supported) applies no balance tilt.

tasks.title: Hand-feel test balance tilt on partial-support resting states
tasks.description: Manually verify on test_track.tscn (or a constructed edge case) that resting precariously now visibly reads as precarious, composition with event lean doesn't look glitchy or fighting, and normal driving on minor bumps/uneven ground doesn't feel twitchy from raycast noise.
tasks.details: No file change -- tuning/verification pass only, adjust VehicleStats balance-tilt knobs from task 12 by feel. Explicit scrutiny item: the corner-raycast approach could be noisy on rough terrain, so check ordinary driving doesn't pick up unwanted jitter, not just the precarious-edge case.
